{{Infobox ancient site|location={{ill|Nara (city)|qid=Q169134}}|part_of={{ill|Gosashi Kofun|qid=Q5587136}}; {{ill|Hishage Kofun|qid=Q11330004}}; {{ill|Ichiniwa Kofun|qid=Q11480471}}; {{ill|Konabe Kofun|qid=Q11302279}}; {{ill|Maezuka Kofun|qid=Q11339900}}; {{ill|Saki Hyōtanyama Kofun|qid=Q11383488}}; {{ill|Saki Ishizukayama Kofun|qid=Q11383491}}; {{ill|Saki Misasagiyama Kofun|qid=Q11383490}}; {{ill|Saki Takatsuka Kofun|qid=Q27898021}}; {{ill|Shiozuka Kofun|qid=Q11428650}}; {{ill|Uwanabe Kofun|qid=Q11289362}}; {{ill|Yomondo Maruzuka Kofun|qid=Q11626337}}}}
'''Saki Tatenami Kofun Group''' (佐紀盾列古墳群)<ref>Some sources read this as "Saki Tatami" ([http://www.kashikoken.jp/museum/yamatonoiseki/kofun/sakimisasagiyama.html Kashihara Archaeological Institute website], etc.).</ref> is a kofun group located in the northwestern part of {{ill|Nara (city)|en|Nara (city)|qid=Q169134|lt=Nara City}}, on the southwestern slopes of the {{ill|Nara Hills|ja|奈良丘陵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nara Hills|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, west of the {{ill|Saho River|ja|佐保川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saho River|qq=}}. Constructed during the late Early to Middle {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|qid=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}}, it includes many royal tombs associated with the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|ja_comment=|2=ja|3=ヤマト王権|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2658252}}.
== Overview ==
[[File:Sakitatenami kohungun aerial 2.jpg|thumb|300px|{{ill|Gosashi Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (top left), {{ill|Saki Ishizukayama Kofun|ja|佐紀石塚山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saki Ishizukayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Saki Ishizukayama Kofun|qq=}} (bottom center), {{ill|Saki Misasagiyama Kofun|ja|佐紀陵山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saki Ryoyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Saki Misasagiyama Kofun|qq=}} (bottom right), and {{ill|Saki Takatsuka Kofun|ja|佐紀高塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saki Takatsuka Kofun|qq=}} (bottom) ({{National Air Photograph}})]]
[[File:Sakitatenami kohungun aerial 1.jpg|thumb|300px|{{ill|Hishage Kofun|lt=Hishage Kofun|lt=Hishiage Kofun|ja|ヒシアゲ古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hishiage Kofun|qq=}} (top left), {{ill|Konabe Kofun|ja|コナベ古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konabe Kofun|qq=}} (bottom center), and {{ill|Uwanabe Kofun|ja|ウワナベ古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uwanabe Kofun|qq=}} (bottom right) ({{National Air Photograph}})]]
[[File:Yodo River and Yamato River Basins.svg|300px|thumb|right|Geographical relationships of the Saki Tatenami Kofun Group and other kofun groups]]
The kofun group, situated on the southern slopes of the {{ill|Narayama Hills|ja|佐紀丘陵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saki Hills|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 平城山丘陵|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11482305}}, was actively used during the late 4th to early 5th century, spanning the late Early to Middle Kofun period. The group includes three colossal keyhole-shaped kofun from the late Early period and four more from the Middle period. These are likely royal tombs of the early {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト政権|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Kingship|ja_comment=|2=ja|3=ヤマト王権|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2658252}}.
During this era, the Yamato Kingship transitioned from the {{ill|Makimuku Kofun Cluster|lt=Makimuku Kofun Cluster|lt=Makimuku Kofun Group|ja|纏向古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Makimuku Kofun Group|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 纒向古墳群}} and {{ill|Yanagimoto Kofun Cluster|lt=Yanagimoto Kofun Cluster|lt=Yamato-Yanagimoto Kofun Group|ja|柳本古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato-Yanagimoto Kofun Group|qq=}}, located in the southeastern Nara Basin, to the Saki Tatenami Kofun Group, which saw the construction of massive kofun. However, by the late Middle period in the late 5th century, the group declined.
The kofun in this group are characterized by keyhole-shaped mounds without distinct paddle-shaped frontal sections.
== Origin of the Name ==
The name originates from the designations of two prominent kofun: {{ill|Gosashi Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} and {{ill|Saki Ishizukayama Kofun|ja|佐紀石塚山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saki Ishizukayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Saki Ishizukayama Kofun|qq=}}, both identified by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|qid=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} as "Saki Tatenami Mausolea."<ref>For example, the ''{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}}'' describes Emperor Seimu's tomb as being "in Saki Tatami," while the ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}'' specifies "buried in the Saki Tatenami Mausoleum."</ref>
The term "Tatenami" (盾列, "shield alignment") may refer to the shield-like layout of the moats surrounding the keyhole-shaped kofun, which are aligned in a north-south direction with the circular rear mounds to the north and the rectangular frontal sections to the south. It likely developed as a descriptive term after the establishment of {{ill|Heijō-kyō|en|Heijō-kyō|qid=Q862509|lt=Heijō-kyō}}.
Some institutions, such as the {{ill|The Museum, Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Nara Prefecture|en|The Museum, Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Nara Prefecture|qid=Q112961122|lt=Kashihara Archaeological Institute}}, use the historical name "Saki Kofun Group."
== Major Kofun ==
; Northwestern Area (Yamamori-cho)
* {{ill|Gosashi Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (identified as the tomb of {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|qid=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū}}, 276 m, late Early Kofun period)
; Western Area (Yamamori-cho, Saki-cho)
* {{ill|Saki Ishizukayama Kofun|ja|佐紀石塚山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saki Ishizukayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Saki Ishizukayama Kofun|qq=}} (identified as the tomb of {{ill|Emperor Seimu|en|Emperor Seimu|qid=Q316672|lt=Emperor Seimu}}, 220 m, late Early Kofun period)
* {{ill|Saki Misasagiyama Kofun|ja|佐紀陵山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saki Ryoyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Saki Misasagiyama Kofun|qq=}} (identified as the tomb of {{ill|Hibasu-hime|ja|日葉酢媛命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hibasu-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Hibasu-hime|qq=}}, consort of Emperor Suinin, 210 m, late Early Kofun period)
* {{ill|Saki Takatsuka Kofun|ja|佐紀高塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saki Takatsuka Kofun|qq=}} (associated with {{ill|Empress Kōken|ja|称徳天皇|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress Kōken|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 孝謙天皇|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q232955}}, direction of frontal section unknown)
; Eastern Area (Saki-cho, Hokkeji-cho)
* {{ill|Hishage Kofun|lt=Hishage Kofun|lt=Hishiage Kofun|ja|ヒシアゲ古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hishiage Kofun|qq=}} (identified as the tomb of {{ill|Princess Iwa|ja|磐之媛|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Princess Iwa|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 磐之媛命|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1066593}}, 218 m, Middle Kofun period)
* {{ill|Konabe Kofun|ja|コナベ古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konabe Kofun|qq=}} (204 m, Middle Kofun period)
* {{ill|Uwanabe Kofun|ja|ウワナベ古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uwanabe Kofun|qq=}} (265 m, Middle Kofun period)
